note: Learning metadata only. These objects do not authorize, deny, or detect. Splunk does not enforce CTRL-IDENTITY-001 or CTRL-MCP-001.
path_a: TRY IT YOURSELF — construct the search in Splunk Search. Studio tokens are not the fresh LIVE run.id.
path_b: SHOW SOLUTION — copyable SPL from an existing hunt, bound table on canonical REPLAY, explanation, limitations.

investigations.title: Find the experiment
investigations.learning_objective: run.id correlation. Filter quoted agentsec.run.id on index=agentsec_telemetry. One UUID is one experiment. Empty is not SAFE.
prerequisites: a run.id from Attack Service or Investigate specimen
investigations.starter_guidance: Index agentsec_telemetry, sourcetype otel:agentic:json. Filter quoted agentsec.run.id. Count events. Read event.name, hop.index, control.id. Do not search index=*.
investigations.hint_1: Start with index=agentsec_telemetry sourcetype=otel:agentic:json and the quoted field agentsec.run.id. Paste the LIVE run.id from Attack Service, or use the Investigate specimen REPLAY id.
investigations.hint_2: Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY is the governed hunt. Canonical REPLAY BASELINE is b419465c-84d8-4639-8449-34dd99841ba9. Fresh LIVE ids come from Attack Service.
investigations.expected_result_shape: One IDENTITY row for this run.id. workflow.entry /identity/delegate. Event names include control.decision and later mcp.* on hop 1 when the tool is allowed.
investigations.result_explanation: You are looking at the indexed copy of one experiment. run.id is the correlation key. It is not authorization.
investigations.security_interpretation: Finding the run proves correlation. It does not prove the caller was authenticated. Splunk did not mint the run.
investigations.does_not_prove: Finding events does not prove authentication, that the claim was a grant, or that the handler ran. Empty is not SAFE.

investigations.title: Identify the actors
investigations.security_question: Who are the principal, caller, and callee?
investigations.learning_objective: attribution != authentication. Read principal.id, caller_agent_id, callee_agent_id. WHO AUTHENTICATED = NOT PROVEN / NOT MODELED.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the same run.id. Read agentsec.principal.id, agentsec.identity.caller_agent_id, agentsec.identity.callee_agent_id. Confirm applicant-web, acme-agent-advisor-005, acme-agent-fulfillment-006.
investigations.hint_1: Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY columns include identity_principal, identity_caller, identity_callee on the CTRL-IDENTITY-001 row.
investigations.hint_2: These identifiers prove lab attribution. They do not prove OAuth, OIDC, JWT, SPIFFE, human, tenant, or device identity.
investigations.result_explanation: These are coded lab identifiers. They tell you who the runtime attributed. They do not tell you who authenticated.
investigations.security_interpretation: CALLER ID != GRANT. AGENT ID STRING != CRYPTOGRAPHIC IDENTITY.
investigations.does_not_prove: The caller cryptographically authenticated. The principal is a verified human. Tenant identity. Device identity.

investigations.title: Inspect the delegation claim
investigations.learning_objective: claim != grant. Read claimed_scope / claimed tool / claimed resource. ATTACK and RETEST share the privileged claim. BASELINE claims policy:read.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the same run.id. Read agentsec.delegation.claimed_scope and identity_requested_tool. ATTACK/RETEST claim customer:read / lookup_customer_tier / cust-001.
investigations.hint_1: identity_claimed_scope and identity_requested_tool sit on the CTRL-IDENTITY-001 row of Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY.
investigations.hint_2: ATTACK and RETEST share fingerprint sha256:56179e463b2faf18c056389ebff32a61e346dd0b4010fb82e8826c4508790dfd. BASELINE is sha256:93f1e257a7d6c7660aa8b1d1b980f1509b7da69e215b385ac79c222e1058b3eb.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK/RETEST claimed_scope=customer:read and requested lookup_customer_tier. BASELINE claimed/requested lookup_policy / policy:read.
investigations.result_explanation: The claim is an input. It is not coded_policy(). It is not an AllowTicket.
investigations.does_not_prove: The claim granted the tool. The claim was cryptographically signed. The agents already possessed customer:read.

investigations.title: Evaluate identity trust
investigations.learning_objective: OBSERVE != ALLOW. Expected OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant untrusted_claim on BASELINE, ATTACK, and RETEST.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the same run.id. Filter CTRL-IDENTITY-001. Read control.decision and control.reason. Confirm claim.trust=untrusted_claim.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-AUTHZ lists control.decision rows. Hop 0 is CTRL-IDENTITY-001. Hop 1 is CTRL-MCP-001 when a follow-on exists.
investigations.hint_2: IDENTITY never ALLOWs the tool and never DENYs the tool. Overlay minting is a separate labeled vulnerable path consumed only by CTRL-MCP-001.
investigations.expected_result_shape: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant. claim.trust=untrusted_claim. Same on ATTACK and RETEST.
investigations.result_explanation: The identity control recorded the trust boundary. It did not mint a grant.
investigations.security_interpretation: OBSERVE != ALLOW. OBSERVE != DENY. IDENTITY CLAIM != AUTHENTICATION.
investigations.does_not_prove: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 authorized the tool. CTRL-IDENTITY-001 blocked the tool. The caller was verified.

investigations.title: Inspect actual coded authority
investigations.security_question: What authority did the agents really possess?
investigations.learning_objective: server-owned authority. Both caller and callee have lookup_policy / policy:read / lending-basics. Neither has lookup_customer_tier or customer:read. A + B != NEW AUTHORITY.
investigations.starter_guidance: Read mcp_coded_allowed_scope on the CTRL-MCP-001 row. Compare to identity_claimed_scope. Coded policy is not in Splunk as allowed_tools.
investigations.hint_1: Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY column mcp_coded_allowed_scope is the coded grant observed on the MCP hop. agentsec.mcp.allowed_tools is prohibited.
investigations.hint_2: Runtime coded_policy() is lookup_policy only. The Attack Service response also reports server_owned_allowed_tools. Do not infer a union of imagined permissions.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Coded allowed scope on MCP hop is policy:read when the request is lookup_policy. Privileged ATTACK/RETEST requested customer:read which is not coded.
investigations.result_explanation: Actual authority is server-owned. The claim asked for more than either agent possesses.
investigations.security_interpretation: A + B != NEW AUTHORITY. A delegation claim must not create authority that neither party possesses.
investigations.does_not_prove: Splunk listed every grant. The overlay is a coded grant. Agent names confer customer:read.

investigations.title: Find the privileged request
investigations.learning_objective: request != grant. ATTACK/RETEST request lookup_customer_tier / customer:read / cust-001. BASELINE requests lookup_policy / policy:read / lending-basics.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the same run.id. Read identity_requested_tool, identity_requested_scope, mcp_tool, mcp_requested_scope, mcp_resource_observation.
investigations.hint_1: Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY already reconstructs the requested triple. Q-MCP-TOOL shows mcp.started only — missing start is not automatically DENY.
investigations.hint_2: mcp.resource.id may be mcp.resource.id_not_indexed_on_this_control_hop. Runtime request remains authoritative for cust-001.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK/RETEST requested lookup_customer_tier customer:read. BASELINE requested lookup_policy policy:read.
investigations.result_explanation: A request was formed. Formation is not authorization and not execution.
investigations.security_interpretation: REQUEST != GRANT. The privileged triple is the attack input, not the grant.
investigations.does_not_prove: The tool was granted because it was requested. Resource id in Splunk is complete. Request proves execution.

investigations.title: Determine who authorized it
investigations.learning_objective: identity control != tool PDP. ATTACK: ALLOW via labeled overlay. RETEST: DENY tool_not_granted. IDENTITY still OBSERVE on both.
investigations.starter_guidance: Filter CTRL-MCP-001 on this run.id. Read decision and reason. Compare ATTACK vs RETEST. Confirm hop 0 is still IDENTITY OBSERVE.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-AUTHZ. ATTACK reason includes vulnerable_profile_fail_open:caller_identity_derived_authority. RETEST reason is tool_not_granted.
investigations.hint_2: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 did not ALLOW the tool. Splunk did not ALLOW the tool. The overlay is lab-only and does not mutate coded_policy().
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW. RETEST CTRL-MCP-001 DENY tool_not_granted. IDENTITY OBSERVE on both.
investigations.result_explanation: The tool PDP decided. The identity control only classified the claim.
investigations.security_interpretation: identity control != tool PDP. Overlay ALLOW is labeled vulnerable behavior, not authenticated identity.
investigations.does_not_prove: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 granted the tool. Splunk denied RETEST. The overlay is a production grant.

investigations.title: Determine whether execution occurred
investigations.learning_objective: ALLOW != execution. Runtime handler count is authoritative. ATTACK handler 1. RETEST handler 0. BASELINE lookup_customer_tier 0 and lookup_policy 1.
investigations.starter_guidance: Search mcp.started / mcp.completed on this run.id. Read Q-MCP-EXECUTED. Then compare runtime lookup_customer_tier_handler_count from Attack Service.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-TOOL is mcp.started only. Q-MCP-EXECUTED joins control + mcp.* into execution_state. execution_observation on Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY is indexed corroboration.
investigations.hint_2: Runtime: ATTACK lookup_customer_tier 1. RETEST 0. Missing Splunk rows are corroboration only. Missing event is not prevention.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK shows mcp.started for lookup_customer_tier. RETEST shows no_indexed_followon_execution_event or equivalent absence. Runtime counts remain authoritative.
investigations.result_explanation: ALLOW is a decision. Execution begins at mcp.started. Handler count proves whether the privileged function ran.
investigations.security_interpretation: ALLOW != EXECUTION. Runtime handler count is authoritative for non-execution.
investigations.does_not_prove: Missing Splunk row means blocked. mcp.completed is authorization. ALLOW means the handler ran.

investigations.title: Compare ATTACK and RETEST
investigations.security_question: What stayed the same and what changed?
investigations.learning_objective: SAME PRINCIPAL. SAME CALLER. SAME CALLEE. SAME DELEGATION CLAIM. SAME PRIVILEGED REQUEST. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. DIFFERENT EXECUTION.
investigations.starter_guidance: Compare principal, caller, callee, claimed scope, requested tool/scope/resource, request fingerprint, IDENTITY OBSERVE. Then compare profile, CTRL-MCP-001, handler count.
investigations.hint_1: Q-AGENT-DELEGATION-AUTHORITY on each run.id. Fingerprint sha256:56179e463b2faf18c056389ebff32a61e346dd0b4010fb82e8826c4508790dfd must match.
investigations.hint_2: Canonical REPLAY: ATTACK f846be88-1f9d-4dde-ac80-193c01b47660 / RETEST 271695f5-4739-44f2-8bf4-0749d04f4b03. Fresh LIVE launches mint new run.ids with the same claim.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Same actors, same claim, same privileged request, same IDENTITY OBSERVE. Different profile, different MCP decision, different execution.
investigations.result_explanation: Equivalence is the frozen request. The discriminator is server-owned ExperimentContext profile feeding CTRL-MCP-001.
investigations.security_interpretation: SAME IDENTITY CLAIM. SAME DELEGATION CLAIM. SAME PRIVILEGED REQUEST. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. DIFFERENT EXECUTION. Splunk observed the difference. Splunk did not cause it.
investigations.does_not_prove: Matching fingerprints mean compromise. One RETEST is universal delegation resistance. Splunk blocked RETEST. IDENTITY denied RETEST.

investigations.title: What can you prove?
investigations.security_question: Which claims are SUPPORTED, CORROBORATED, NOT PROVEN, or INCORRECT?
investigations.learning_objective: Classify findings. Prohibit caller-id-proves-authentication, claim-is-grant, IDENTITY-granted-the-tool, Splunk-denied, A-plus-B-inherits-union.
investigations.starter_guidance: Write four columns: SUPPORTED / CORROBORATED / NOT PROVEN / INCORRECT. Use runtime handler counts as authoritative for execution. Use Splunk as a copy.
investigations.hint_1: SUPPORTED: identifiers present; delegation claim; IDENTITY OBSERVE untrusted; privileged request; MCP decision; handler execution/non-execution; same request across ATTACK and RETEST.
investigations.hint_2: INCORRECT: caller_agent_id proves authentication; delegation claim grants authority; CTRL-IDENTITY-001 granted the tool; Splunk denied the request; Agent A + Agent B inherit the union of imagined permissions. NOT PROVEN: cryptographic caller identity, OAuth, OIDC, SPIFFE, human identity, tenant identity, every delegation attack is prevented, missing event proves prevention.
investigations.expected_result_shape: A classification table you wrote, not a detector output.
investigations.result_explanation: Evidence discipline is the skill. Dashboards do not decide truth.
investigations.security_interpretation: Authoritative: runtime IDENTITY classification, MCP decision, and handler counts on this experiment. Corroborative: Splunk copy when complete. Splunk is not enforcement.
investigations.does_not_prove: Cryptographic identity, production detector coverage, or that blocking all delegation would have been the correct control.
